newsitem.title: DUBAI: United Arab Emirates shares rise in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: United Arab Emirates shares rise in moderate trade.

text.p: The index on the United Arab Emirates' unofficial stock market rose 12.77 points in moderate trade in the week to Thursday, brokers said.
The National Bank of Abu Dhabi (NBAD) index rose some half a percent to 2,579.35 from 2,566.58 points. Of the 27 traded firms, shares of six rose, three dropped and the rest were flat.

Brokers said trade was moderate as investors waited for news on public offerings of two new companies, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank and Oasis International Leasing Co. The UAE government recently announced their formation.
Among the main gainers were the Abu Dhabi National Hotels Co, which gained two dirhams to 115, and NBAD and Al Ain Al-Ahlia Insurance rose 10 dirhams each to 680 and 960 dirhams.
Market leader Etisalat, the UAE's telecommunications company, chalked up five dirhams to end the week at 985.
Abu Dhabi National Insurance gathered 10 dirhams to end the week at 1,100. Similarly, National Bank of Dubai moved up 10 dirhams to 680.
Al-Khazna Insurance extended recent losses, slipping 10 dirhams to 265 after having lost 15 dirhams the previous week.
Shares in the new Emaar Properties were unchanged at 17 dirhams after slipping five dirhams the previous week.
Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank was unchanged at 350 and Union National Bank remained at 360 dirhams.
